extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance from the MPEP on handling Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs), preparation/content of Office actions, citation and rejection standards, and related form usage and procedures for patent examiners and applicants/agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments without amendment or factual showing ineffective after Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission containing arguments without either amendment of the rejected claims or the submission of a showing of facts will not be effective to remove such rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board decision has res judicata / 'law of the case' effect in that application and related applications (see MPEP §§ 706.03(w) and 1214.01). Simply re-arguing without amendment or new facts will not overcome a Board rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use form paragraph 7.42.07 when appeal withdrawn and prosecution reopened
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.42.07 should be used to notify applicant that the appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution has been reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when an RCE (with required fee and submission) is timely filed after a Board decision but before further appeal or civil action, resulting in withdrawal of the appeal under 37 CFR 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for RCE under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice does not apply to provisional, design applications, utility/plant filed before June 8, 1995, or patents under reexamination (see 37 CFR 1.114(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE requires timely submission and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114 must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission as required by 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fee and submission are timely filed, the appeal is withdrawn pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 and prosecution is reopened; the submission filed with the RCE will be entered if proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision (missing fee/submission) — notify using form paragraph 7.42.16
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but before further appeal or civil action and the RCE lacks the fee and/or the submission, the examiner should notify the applicant that the RCE is improper by using form paragraph 7.42.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time for seeking court review has passed, include the form paragraph with Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment as appropriate; if time remains, include on PTOL-90. Do not set a time period. If a submission accompanies the RCE but fee is missing, state whether the submission has been entered (generally it should not be entered unless it obviously places the application in condition for allowance with SPE approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use form paragraph 7.42.16 for ineligible application types; use PTO-2051 instead
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.42.16 should not be used if the application is not a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case, prepare and mail 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE),' Form PTO-2051, by technical support personnel to notify applicant that continued examination does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule on entering submissions filed with improper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, if a submission was filed with an improper RCE, it should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: an amendment which obviously places the application in condition for allowance may be entered with supervisory patent examiner approval. See MPEP § 1214.07 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE practice after court review is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure set forth in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available after the filing of a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or the commencement of a civil action, unless the appeal/civil action is terminated and the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed in an application that underwent court review, the examiner should bring the application to the SPE or special program examiner to determine if the RCE is proper. Termination of an unsuccessful appeal or civil action generally results in abandonment unless the application contains allowed claims or the court's mandate directs further Office action. See MPEP § 1216.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Form PTO/SB/30 for RCE transmittal and follow its instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/30, 'Request for Continued Examination (RCE) Transmittal,' may be used by applicant for filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 and contains required information and warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form instructs that RCE practice does not apply to certain application types, that RCE is not a new application and will not change filing date, that a submission and fee are required, and warns against including credit card info on the form. Instruction sheet (not submitted) further explains filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing qualifications: prosecution must be closed
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution in the application must be closed to file an RCE. Prosecution is closed if application is under appeal, or the last Office action is a final action, notice of allowance, or an action that otherwise closes prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.114(b). If prosecution is not closed, RCE is improper. A request for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(c) does not satisfy the submission requirement for an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement for RCE (what counts as submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission and a fee are required at the time the RCE is filed. If reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet 37 CFR 1.111 reply requirements. If no outstanding Office action, the submission can be an IDS, an amendment, new arguments, new evidence, or a previously filed amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously submitted amendments (e.g., amendment after final rejection) may be used; if a final Office action is outstanding, amendments filed after the final may be considered submissions even if not checked on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE will not toll statutory or other time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RCE is improper (e.g., prosecution not closed or submission/fee not filed) it will NOT toll any time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before appeal: time in last Office action continues to run and application may be abandoned if reply not timely filed; Under appeal: an improper RCE withdraws the appeal, leading to allowance or abandonment depending on claim status. No additional time will be given to correct an improper RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must make a thorough study and investigation (37 CFR 1.104(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application, the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention. The examination shall be complete as to compliance with statutes/rules and patentability as claimed, as well as matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should examine both substantive and formal aspects and limit action only in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder, fundamental defects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action must state reasons for adverse action (37 CFR 1.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated in an Office action and such information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the applicant to judge the propriety of continuing the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient explanation and references so the applicant can assess whether to continue prosecution; in pro se cases or exceptional situations a more complete explanation may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When rejecting for novelty/obviousness cite best references and explain pertinence (37 CFR 1.104(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable. The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections, set out how a reference is modified or how plural references are combined. Include particular figures/pages/paragraphs when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may rely on applicant admissions and facts within Office knowledge (37 CFR 1.104(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination), and may rely upon facts within his or her knowledge pursuant to paragraph (d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on facts within Office employee's personal knowledge, the data must be as specific as possible and may require an affidavit to support the data (subject to contradiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third-party-developed subject matter as prior art and joint research agreement treatment (37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)-(3)(i-iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To overcome a 103 rejection based on 102(e)/(f)/(g) prior art via 103(c)(2), the applicant must provide a statement that the prior art and the claimed invention were made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement (as defined) that was in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made, and that the invention was made as a result of activities within the scope of that agreement; define 'joint research agreement' per the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusion by statutory invention registration (waiver) for original and reissue applications (37 CFR 1.104(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in any original application naming an inventor will be rejected as being precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed. Similar preclusion applies in reissue applications under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue, the preclusion applies where the reissue seeks to claim subject matter not covered by prior-issued claims and that was waived in the statutory invention registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements (37 CFR 1.104(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner cites domestic patents, numbers and dates and names of patentees will be stated; for domestic patent application publications, publication number, publication date, and applicant names; for foreign published applications/patents, nationality, numbers, dates, and patentee names. For printed publications provide author, title, date, pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only part of a document is involved, identify particular pages/sheets. Provide sufficient bibliographic detail to enable identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for facts within personal knowledge of Office employees (37 CFR 1.104(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an employee of the Office, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee, subject to contradiction or explanation by applicant's affidavits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to support factual assertions with sworn statements if challenged by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be stated when record unclear (37 CFR 1.104(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record of prosecution does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning; reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of separate communication. The applicant may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure by the examiner to respond to any such applicant statement does not give rise to any implication. Provide clear reasoning to maintain transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office actions must include necessary elements and use PTOL-326 for summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Under current procedure the examiner signifies on Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 certain information including period set for reply, attachments, and a 'Summary of Action' describing the position on all claims; attachments (e.g., Notice of References Cited) are part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102 should conclude all actions. Office actions should notify reasons for rejection/objection per 35 U.S.C. 132, include particular figures/pages/paragraphs of references when necessary, and set out how references are modified/combined for 103 rejections. Include application number, 4-digit art unit, examiner's name, and encourage inclusion of the 4-digit confirmation number on every paper filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding contact paragraphs (7.100 / 7.101 / 7.102) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.100, 7.101, or 7.102 at the conclusion of all actions to provide contact information and inquiry instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate brackets with examiner name, telephone number, normal duty hours/days, supervisory contact if examiner unreachable, and follow 5/4/9 or non-5/4/9 schedule guidance for inserting duty days and compressed day off. Include PAIR and EBC contact info as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate detail in Office actions for pro se or unfamiliar inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional cases and in pro se cases where the inventor is unfamiliar with patent law/practice, a more complete explanation in Office actions may be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include additional explanatory material, indicate allowable subject matter, and set out requirements (including restriction/election requirements) in a manner understandable to lay inventors.
